Claire — thanks for the clear asks. Summarizing here so Acme and our internal teams have the same picture.

TL;DR: We can commit to a Jun 18-20 pin-window with the following constraints and owners.

- Timeline: Jun 18 00:00 UTC — Jun 20 23:59 UTC as the pin-window. Cutover will be staged by region; primary cutover for US workload will happen Jun 18 02:00 UTC.
- Rollback window: 48h of monitored rollback is available if quality regressions exceed guardrails (see INF-4821). After 48h, rollback requires a schedule agreement and engineering on-call.
- Owners:
  - Migration orchestration & rollforward/rollback: Priyom Das (prod infra)
  - Risk gating / compatibility exceptions: Irene Choi (product)
  - Customer comms + external notice: Marissa Cole (comms) — Marissa, see the requested customer-facing template item below.

Priyom / Irene / Marissa — can you confirm you accept these owners? I’m attaching the cutover ledger (draft) and a short comms lattice we plan to publish.

Follow-ups I will do: sync with infra on the exact monitoring thresholds (latency and hallucination delta metrics) and add the final rollback play to the ledger by Fri.

Marcus

Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — I accept orchestration ownership. A few product/infra clarifications and asks before I give final signoff:

1) Compatibility shim: Acme noted they still call the legacy v1 embed endpoint for a small fraction of requests. We can keep a soft-bridge for 30 days post-cutover, but only if Acme agrees to a usage cap (<= 5% of baseline traffic). If they exceed the cap we will throttle and surface an alert.

2) Monitoring thresholds: need agreement on the primary quality metric. I propose: top-100 aggregate embedding drift (cosine) and 95th percentile latency. If drift > 0.06 or latency spike > 200ms above baseline for 10 minutes, auto-initiate rollback procedures.

3) Exception intake: Irene, please confirm product gate criteria for granting the compatibility exception and the turnaround SLA for decisions (I suggest 48 hours).

Marissa — for the customer note I suggest two short bullets: what changes (model variant only), how we’ll monitor, and who to contact (redwood-support + acme-dedicated). I can draft the technical appendix for the note.

Priyom
Senior Product Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Planned model update (Jun 18-20) — what to expect
Hi Acme customers,
On Jun 18-20 Redwood will swap to an improved model variant for embedding generation. This is a backend model update only — there are no API path changes and no required client code updates.
What we will monitor:
- Quality: top-100 embedding drift (cosine) and a small evaluation set run hourly during the pin-window.
- Performance: p95 latency and throughput.
Rollback plan:
- If quality or latency crosses agreed thresholds we will initiate an automatic rollback within the 48h monitored window. If rollback is required after the 48h window, we will coordinate schedule with Acme.
Who to contact:
- Redwood support: support@redwood.ai (for incident/status updates)
- Dedicated account contact: Marcus Lin (marcus.lin@redwood.ai) and Acme PM: Claire Jennings (claire.jennings@acme.com)

I’ll attach the short technical appendix (Priyom — please add the monitoring thresholds you recommended) and the runbook sketch from Acme. Once you confirm Marcus / Claire I’ll send the note jointly.
